title: HTTP Datagram Lifecycle and Intermediary Conversion Architecture
purpose: Define RFC 9297 lifecycle and intermediary conversion policy for HTTP Datagrams and DATAGRAM Capsules without coupling the policy to live transport mutation.
design_summary: `Http3DatagramLifecycle` returns explicit send, accept, drop, buffer, or abort decisions for request support, extension overrides, send-side openness, receive-side closure, uncreated streams, HTTP/1.x Capsule Protocol start, and underlying flow-control checks. `Http3DatagramIntermediaryPolicy` validates Capsule payload length consistency, parses DATAGRAM Capsule payloads with HTTP Datagram semantics, avoids full-value buffering, chooses conversion/drop actions for intermediaries, applies extension limits, and records the recommendation that new HTTP Datagram extensions use the Capsule Protocol.
data_and_state_considerations: The slice returns immutable decisions and does not open streams, queue frames, buffer live data, mutate QUIC transport state, or perform proxy forwarding.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Unsupported HTTP Datagram requests map to request-stream abort with H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR.
Closed stream sides silently drop datagrams.
Uncreated but creatable streams can either drop or temporarily buffer for approximately one RTT.
HTTP/1.x Capsule Protocol can start only on the final request on a connection.
Intermediaries require Capsule Protocol identification before re-encoding.
Oversized or extension-disallowed datagrams are dropped without buffering.
risks: This slice intentionally avoids wiring live QUIC DATAGRAM effects into `QuicConnectionRuntime`.
Actual CONNECT-UDP and CONNECT-IP forwarding are left to RFC 9298 and RFC 9484.
Future adapter work must translate these decisions into concrete stream/datagram effects without weakening the pure policy proof.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The lifecycle policy is the handoff point between RFC 9297 semantics and later MASQUE adapters. It keeps core transport ownership separate from HTTP extension semantics.
